title.zh: 卷二十九 唐書5: 莊宗本紀三
title.en: Volume 29 Book of Later Tang 5: Zhuangzong Annals 3
title.raw: 卷二十九 唐書5: 莊宗本紀三 Volume 29 Book of Later Tang 5: Zhuangzong Annals 3

sentences.zh: 天祐十六年春正月，李存審城德勝，夾河為柵。

translations.literal: In spring of Tianyou 16, first month, Li Cunshen walled Desheng and set palisades along both banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianyou 16 Li Cunshen fortified Desheng and ran stockades along both sides of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝還魏州，命昭義軍節度使李嗣昭權知幽州軍府事。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned to Weizhou and ordered Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao to act as provisional administrator of the Youzhou military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu went back to Weizhou and left Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi as acting head of the Youzhou command.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝兼領幽州，遣近臣李紹宏提舉府事。

translations.literal: Third month, the Emperor also took Youzhou in personal charge and sent close attendant Li Shaohong to oversee headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he added Youzhou to his own titles and sent Li Shaohong to run the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，梁將賀瑰圍德勝南城，百道攻擊，復以艨艟扼斷津渡。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Liang general He Gui besieged Desheng's south city, attacking by a hundred routes, and again used mengchong ships to choke the ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month He Gui of Liang invested the south citadel of Desheng from every angle and blocked the crossing with war junks.

sentences.zh: 帝馳而往，陣於北岸。

translations.literal: The Emperor galloped there and drew up battle lines on the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu raced to the scene and formed up on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 南城守將氏延賞告急，且言矢石將盡。

translations.literal: South-city defender Shi Yanbang reported urgency and said arrows and stones were nearly spent.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanbang, who held the south city, begged for relief and warned that missiles were almost gone.

sentences.zh: 帝以重賄召募能破賊艦者，於是獻技者數十，或言能吐火焚舟，或言能禁咒兵刃，悉命試之，無驗。

translations.literal: The Emperor offered heavy bribes to recruit men who could break the enemy ships; then dozens came forward with tricks—some claiming they could spit fire to burn boats, others that they could charm weapons—and he had them all tried, without effect.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu posted rich rewards for anyone who could smash the Liang fleet; dozens came forward, some promising fire-breathing, others weapon-charms, but every trick failed when tested.

sentences.zh: 帝憂形於色，親從都將王建及進曰：「臣請效命。

translations.literal: Worry showed on the Emperor's face; personal follower chief Wang Jianji advanced and said: "Your servant asks to give his life.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu's worry showed plainly; Wang Jianji of the personal guard stepped forward: "Let me try."

sentences.zh: 」乃以巨索連舟十艘，選效節勇士三百人，持斧被鎧，鼓枻而進，至中流。

translations.literal: " He then took huge ropes to link ten boats, chose three hundred Xiaojie braves with axes and armor, beat the oars and advanced to midstream.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed ten boats with heavy cables, picked three hundred loyal guards in mail with axes, and rowed hard into midstream.

sentences.zh: 梁樓船三層，蒙以牛革，懸板為楯。

translations.literal: Liang tower ships were three decks high, covered with oxhide, with hanging boards as shields.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang towers rose three stories, armored in oxhide with plank screens hung as shields.

sentences.zh: 建及率持斧者入艨艟間，斬其竹笮，破其懸楯；

translations.literal: Jianji led the axemen into the mengchong lanes, cut their bamboo lashings, and broke the hanging shields;
translations.idiomatic: Jianji drove the axemen between the war junks, severed their bamboo bindings, and smashed the hanging screens;

sentences.zh: 又於上流取甕數百，用竹笮維之，積薪於上，灌以脂膏，火發亙空；

translations.literal: upstream he also took several hundred jars, bound them with bamboo, piled fuel on top, poured on grease, and fire blazed across the sky;
translations.idiomatic: farther upriver he rigged hundreds of jars on bamboo rafts, heaped fuel, drenched them in oil, and sent flames across the sky;

sentences.zh: 又以巨艦載甲士，令乘煙鼓噪。

translations.literal: he also loaded armored men on great ships and ordered them to shout through the smoke.
translations.idiomatic: then sent great ships full of armored men to roar through the smoke.

sentences.zh: 梁之樓船斷絏而下，沈溺者殆半。

translations.literal: Liang tower ships broke their moorings and drifted down; nearly half sank by drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Liang towers broke their cables and drifted downstream; nearly half the crews drowned.

sentences.zh: 軍既得渡，梁軍乃退。

translations.literal: Once the army could cross, the Liang army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the crossing was open, the Liang force pulled back.

sentences.zh: 命騎軍追襲至濮陽，俘斬千計。

translations.literal: He ordered cavalry to pursue and strike as far as Puyang, capturing and beheading on the order of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry chased them to Puyang and took or killed on the order of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 賀瑰由此飲氣遘疾而卒。

translations.literal: From this He Gui choked on resentment, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui brooded himself into illness and died.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，帝歸晉陽。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Cunxu returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，梁將王瓚帥眾數萬自黎陽渡河，營於楊村，造舟為梁，以通津路。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Liang general Wang Zan led tens of thousands from Liyang across the river, camped at Yangcun, and built boats as bridges to open the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Zan of Liang crossed from Liyang with tens of thousands, camped at Yangcun, and bridged the ford with boats.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，帝自晉陽至魏州，發徒數萬以廣德勝北城，自是，日與梁軍接戰。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Emperor came from Jinyang to Weizhou and mobilized tens of thousands to enlarge Desheng's north city; from this day he clashed with the Liang army daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Cunxu came from Jinyang to Weizhou and drafted tens of thousands to expand the north citadel of Desheng; thereafter he fought Liang every day.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，帝軍於河南，夜伏步兵於潘張村梁軍寨下，以騎軍掠其餉運，擒其斥候。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, wuxu, the Emperor's army lay south of the river; by night he hid foot soldiers below the Liang camp at Panzhang village, used cavalry to raid their grain convoys, and seized their scouts.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the twelfth month he camped south of the river, hid infantry under the Liang camp at Panzhang by night, raided their supply trains with horse, and seized scouts.

sentences.zh: 梁王瓚結陣以待，帝軍以鐵騎突之，諸軍繼進，梁軍大奔，赴水死者甚眾，瓚走保北城。

translations.literal: Liang's Wang Zan formed ranks to await them; the Emperor's army burst them with iron cavalry, the rest followed, the Liang army fled in great rout, many drowned in the water, and Zan fled to hold the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zan of Liang drew up to meet him; iron cavalry smashed the line, the whole host piled in, Liang broke and many drowned, and Zan fled into the north citadel.

sentences.zh: 天祐十七年春，幽州民於田中得金印，文曰：「關中龜印」，李紹宏獻於行台。

translations.literal: Spring of Tianyou 17, in Youzhou a farmer found a gold seal in his field with the inscription "Guanzhong turtle seal"; Li Shaohong presented it to the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianyou 17 a farmer near Youzhou dug up a gold seal reading "Guanzhong turtle seal," which Li Shaohong sent to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，梁將劉鄩、尹皓寇同州。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao raided Tong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Liang struck Tong.

sentences.zh: 先是，河中節度使朱友謙取同州，以其子令德主留務，請梁主降節。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hezhong military commissioner Zhu Youqian had taken Tong and left his son Lingde in charge of remaining affairs, begging the Liang ruler to confirm his commission.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Youqian of Hezhong had seized Tong, left his son Lingde to govern, and asked Liang to confirm his post.

sentences.zh: 梁主怒，不與，遂請旄節於帝。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler was angry and refused; Zhu Youqian then asked the Emperor for a commission.
translations.idiomatic: Liang refused in anger, so Youqian turned to Cunxu for a banner.

sentences.zh: 梁主乃遣劉鄩與華州節度使尹皓帥兵圍同州，友謙來告難，帝遣蕃漢總管李存審、昭義節度使李嗣昭、代州刺史王建及率師赴援。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler then sent Liu Yan and Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao with troops to besiege Tong; Youqian reported the crisis, and the Emperor sent Chinese-and-tribal overall commander Li Cunshen, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, and Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji with armies to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Huazhou to invest Tong; Youqian cried for help, and Cunxu sent Li Cunshen as overall commander, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, and Wang Jianji of Dai to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 九月，師至河中，朝至夕濟，梁人不意王師之至，望之大駭。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the armies reached Hezhong; they crossed in the morning and by evening were over— the Liang men did not expect the royal army and were greatly terrified on seeing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the relief force reached Hezhong, crossed at dawn and were ashore by dusk; Liang had not expected Jin troops and panicked at the sight.

sentences.zh: 明日約戰，與朱友謙謀，遲明，進軍距梁壘；

translations.literal: Next day they agreed to battle; consulting with Zhu Youqian, at first light they advanced and drew near the Liang ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: The next day they offered battle; after counsel with Youqian they moved at first light and closed on the Liang camp;

sentences.zh: 梁人悉眾以出，蒲人在南，王師在北。

translations.literal: the Liang men came out with their full host; Pu men were on the south, the royal army on the north.
translations.idiomatic: Liang came out in full strength with Pu allies on the south and the Jin host on the north.

sentences.zh: 騎軍既接，蒲人小卻，李嗣昭以輕騎抗之，梁軍奔潰，追斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: Once the cavalry engaged, the Pu men gave a little ground; Li Sizhao met them with light horse and the Liang army broke and fled; more than two thousand were cut down in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When horse met horse the Pu line wavered; Li Sizhao hit them with light cavalry, Liang collapsed, and over two thousand fell in the chase.

sentences.zh: 是夜，劉鄩收餘眾保營，自是閉壁不出。

translations.literal: That night Liu Yan gathered the remnant and held camp; from then on they shut the walls and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: That night Liu Yan pulled the survivors into camp and never came out again.

sentences.zh: 數日，鄩遂宵遁。

translations.literal: After several days Yan fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Yan slipped away by night.

sentences.zh: 王師追及於渭河，所棄兵仗輜重不可勝計，劉鄩、尹皓單騎獲免。

translations.literal: The royal army caught them at the Wei River; abandoned arms, gear, and baggage were beyond counting, and Liu Yan and Yin Hao alone on horseback escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jin caught them at the Wei; abandoned weapons and wagons littered the bank, while Yan and Yin rode off alone.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鄩憂恚發病而卒。

translations.literal: Before long Yan died of grief and vexation that brought on illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yan died of shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 王師略地至奉先，嗣昭因謁唐帝諸陵而還。

translations.literal: The royal army overran the land as far as Fengxian; Sizhao on the way visited the tombs of the Tang emperors and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin columns swept to Fengxian; Sizhao paid respects at the Tang imperial tombs on the march home.

sentences.zh: 天祐十八年春正月，魏州開元寺僧傳真獲傳國寶，獻於行台。

translations.literal: Spring of Tianyou 18, first month, a monk of Weizhou's Kaiyuan Temple named Chuanzhen obtained the dynastic heirloom seal and presented it to the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianyou 18 the Kaiyuan monk Chuanzhen at Weizhou found the heirloom seal and sent it to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 驗其文，即「受命於天，子孫寶之」八字也，群僚稱賀。

translations.literal: Examining the inscription, it was exactly the eight characters "Mandated by Heaven—may sons and grandsons treasure it"; the officials all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The characters proved to be the eight words "Mandated by Heaven—may sons and grandsons treasure it," and the staff hailed the omen.

sentences.zh: 傳真師於廣明中，遇京師喪亂得之，秘藏已四十年矣。

translations.literal: Chuanzhen said that in the Guangming era, amid the capital's turmoil, he had obtained it and kept it hidden for forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzhen said he had taken it during the Guangming disorders and kept it secret for forty years.

sentences.zh: 篆文古體，人不之識，至是獻之。

translations.literal: The seal script was ancient and none could read it; only now was it presented.
translations.idiomatic: The archaic seal script had baffled everyone until he brought it forward.

sentences.zh: 時淮南楊溥、四川王衍皆遣使致書，勸帝嗣唐帝位，帝不從。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Pu of Huainan and Wang Yan of Sichuan both sent envoys with letters urging the Emperor to succeed to the Tang throne; the Emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu of Huainan and Wang Yan of Shu both wrote urging Cunxu to take the Tang throne; he refused.

sentences.zh: 二月，代州刺史王建及卒。

translations.literal: Second month, Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Wang Jianji of Dai died.

sentences.zh: 是月，鎮州大將張文禮殺其帥王鎔。

translations.literal: That month a great Zhen officer, Zhang Wenli, killed his commander Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Wenli, a senior Zhen commander, murdered his lord Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 時帝方與諸將宴，酒酣樂作，聞鎔遇弑，遽投觶而泣曰：「趙王與吾把臂同盟，分如金石，何負於人，覆宗絕祀，冤哉！

translations.literal: The Emperor was then feasting with his generals; when the music was loud and the wine deep he heard that Rong had been assassinated, abruptly cast aside his cup and wept, saying: "Prince Zhao clasped arms with me in alliance, our bond like metal and stone—what wrong did he do anyone, that his house is destroyed and his line cut off? What injustice!
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu was drinking with his officers when word came that Rong had been killed; he flung down his cup and wept: "The Prince of Zhao was my sworn brother, our bond iron-hard—what had he done to anyone, that his clan is wiped out? Monstrous wrong!

sentences.zh: 」先是，滹沱暴漲，漂關城之半，溺死者千計。

translations.literal: " Earlier the Hutuo had flooded violently, washing away half the pass city; those drowned numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier the Hutuo had burst and swept away half the frontier town, drowning thousands.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天西北有赤昆如血，占者言趙分之災，至是果驗。

translations.literal: That year in the northwest sky a crimson vapor like blood appeared; diviners said it foretold disaster for Zhao territory—and now it was fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: That year a blood-red cloud hung in the northwest; seers called it Zhao's doom—and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 時張文禮遣使請旄節於帝，帝曰：「 文禮之罪，期於無赦，敢邀予旄節！

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli then sent envoys begging a commission from the Emperor; the Emperor said: "Wenli's crime admits no pardon—how dare he ask my banner!
translations.idiomatic: Wenli then asked Cunxu for a commission; Cunxu said, "Wenli deserves no mercy—how dare he ask for my seal!

sentences.zh: 」左右曰：「方今事繁，不欲與人生事。

translations.literal: " Those beside him said: "Affairs are pressing now; we do not wish to pick another fight.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants said, "Matters are urgent—we should not pick another fight.

sentences.zh: 」帝不得已而從之，乃承製授文禮鎮州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had no choice but to agree and, by imperial rescript, made Wenli Zhenzhou military commissioner in temporary charge.
translations.idiomatic: " Cunxu yielded and, by rescript, confirmed Wenli as acting military commissioner of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 三月，河中節度使朱友謙、昭義節度使李嗣昭、滄州節度使李存審、定州節度使王處直、邢州節度使李嗣源、成德軍兵馬留後張文禮、遙領天平軍節度使閻寶、大同軍節度使李存璋、新州節度使王鬱、振武節度使李存進、同州節度使朱令德，各遣使勸進，請帝紹唐帝位，帝報書不允。

translations.literal: Third month, Hezhong commissioner Zhu Youqian, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, Cangzhou commissioner Li Cunshen, Dingzhou commissioner Wang Chuzhi, Xingzhou commissioner Li Siyuan, Chengde army acting commander Zhang Wenli, distant Taiping army commissioner Yan Bao, Datong commissioner Li Cunzhang, Xinzhou commissioner Wang Yu, Zhenwu commissioner Li Cunjin, and Tongzhou commissioner Zhu Lingde each sent envoys urging advancement and asking the Emperor to succeed to the Tang throne; the Emperor replied in writing that he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Youqian of Hezhong, Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Cunshen of Cangzhou, Chuzhi of Ding, Siyuan of Xing, Wenli acting for Chengde, Yan Bao holding Taiping in title, Cunzhang of Datong, Yu of Xin, Cunjin of Zhenwu, and Lingde of Tong all urged Cunxu to take the throne; he wrote back refusing.

sentences.zh: 自是，諸鎮凡三上章勸進，各獻貨幣數十萬，以助即位之費，帝左右亦勸帝早副人望，帝撝挹久之。

translations.literal: From this the circuits thrice submitted memorials urging advancement, each presenting several hundred thousand in goods and coin to help the cost of enthronement; those beside the Emperor also urged him early to satisfy public expectation; the Emperor modestly declined for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the circuits petitioned three times, each sending hundreds of thousands in goods toward the coronation; his courtiers pressed him to satisfy the realm; Cunxu demurred again and again.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙季良傳》：季良嘗蘿手扶御座，自謂輔佐之象，由是頗述天時人事以諷，莊宗深納其言。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals · Biography of Zhao Jiliang》 says: Jiliang once steadied the imperial seat with a creeping hand and took it as a sign he was meant to aid the throne; from this he often spoke of Heaven's seasons and human affairs by way of hint, and Zhuangzong took his words deeply to heart.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals · Biography of Zhao Jiliang》 records that Jiliang once steadied the throne with his hand on the armrest, calling it a sign of ministerial destiny, and often hinted at Heaven and policy until Zhuangzong embraced his counsel.)〉

sentences.zh: 秋七月，河東節度副使盧汝弼卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Hedong deputy military commissioner Lu Rubi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Lu Rubi, deputy commissioner of Hedong, died.

sentences.zh: 八月庚申，令天平節度使閻寶、成德兵馬留後符習率兵討張文禮於鎮州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, gengshen, ordered Taiping commissioner Yan Bao and Chengde acting commander Fu Xi to lead troops against Zhang Wenli at Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the eighth month Yan Bao of Taiping and Fu Xi, acting commander of Chengde, marched on Wenli at Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初，王鎔令偏將符習以本部兵從帝屯於德勝。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Rong had ordered subordinate general Fu Xi to bring his own troops with the Emperor's camp at Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had earlier detached Fu Xi with his own command to serve at Desheng under Cunxu.

sentences.zh: 文禮既行弑逆，忌鎔故將，多被誅戮，因遣使聞於帝，欲以他兵代習歸鎮，習等懼，請留。

translations.literal: After Wenli's regicide he feared Rong's old officers and many were executed; he therefore sent word to the Emperor wishing other troops to replace Xi and return to Zhen, and Xi and the rest were afraid and asked to stay.
translations.idiomatic: After the murder Wenli purged Rong's veterans and asked Cunxu to swap other troops for Fu Xi's return; Xi and his men, in fear, begged to remain.

sentences.zh: 帝令傳旨於習及別將趙仁貞、烏震等，明正文禮弑逆之罪，且言：「爾等荷戟從征，蓋君父之故，銜冤報恩，誰人無心。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent word to Xi and the other commanders Zhao Renzhen and Wu Zhen, stating Wenli's regicide plainly and saying: "You bore arms on campaign for father and lord; who lacks a heart to repay a wrong with gratitude?
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu sent orders to Xi, Zhao Renzhen, and Wu Zhen, spelling out Wenli's crime and saying, "You marched for lord and father—who would not want vengeance?

sentences.zh: 吾當給爾資糧，助爾兵甲，爾試思之！

translations.literal: I shall give you provisions and aid you with arms—think on it!
translations.idiomatic: I will feed you and arm you—think on it!

sentences.zh: 」於是習等率諸將三十餘人，慟哭於牙門，請討文禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xi and more than thirty other commanders wept at headquarters and begged to punish Wenli.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and thirty-odd officers wept at the gate and begged leave to punish Wenli.

sentences.zh: 帝因授習成德軍兵馬留後，以部下鎮、冀兵致討於文禮；

translations.literal: The Emperor then appointed Xi acting Chengde army commander and sent the Zhen and Ji troops under him against Wenli;
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu made Xi acting commander of Chengde and sent the Zhen and Ji columns against Wenli;

sentences.zh: 又遣閻寶以助之，以史建瑭為前鋒。

translations.literal: he also sent Yan Bao to help, with Shi Jiantang as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao followed to assist, with Shi Jiantang in the van.

sentences.zh: 甲子，攻趙州，刺史王鋌送符印以迎，閻寶遂引軍至鎮州城下，營於西北隅。

translations.literal: On jiazi they attacked Zhao prefecture; prefect Wang Di surrendered his seal to welcome them; Yan Bao then led the army to below the walls of Zhen and camped at the northwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi they took Zhao; Prefect Wang Di handed over his seal; Yan Bao then pitched camp below Zhen's northwest wall.

sentences.zh: 是月，張文禮病疽而卒，其子處瑾代掌軍事。

translations.literal: That month Zhang Wenli died of carbuncle; his son Chujin took command.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wenli died of a boil; his son Chujin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 九月，前鋒將史建瑭與鎮人戰於城下，為流矢所中而卒。

translations.literal: Ninth month, vanguard Shi Jiantang fought the Zhen men below the walls and was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shi Jiantang fought under the walls and fell to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己未，梁將戴思遠攻德勝北城，帝命李嗣源設伏於戚城，令騎軍挑戰。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, jiwei, Liang general Dai Siyuan attacked Desheng's north city; the Emperor ordered Li Siyuan to set an ambush at Qi city and sent cavalry to challenge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the tenth month Dai Siyuan of Liang struck Desheng's north citadel; Cunxu had Li Siyuan lie in wait at Qi and sent horse to provoke.

sentences.zh: 梁軍大至，帝御中軍以禦之。

translations.literal: The Liang army came in force; the Emperor took the center army to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang massed, Cunxu took the center himself.

sentences.zh: 時李從珂偽為梁幟，奔入梁壘，斧其眺樓，持級而還。

translations.literal: At that time Li Congke feigned Liang banners, charged into the Liang camp, chopped down their watchtower, and returned with heads.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congke rode in under false Liang colors, smashed a watchtower in their camp, and came back with heads.

sentences.zh: 梁軍愈恐，步兵漸至，李嗣源以鐵騎三千乘之，梁軍大敗，俘斬二萬計。

translations.literal: The Liang army grew more fearful; as foot soldiers arrived, Li Siyuan struck with three thousand iron horse; the Liang army was routed and more than twenty thousand were captured or beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liang wavered; when their foot came up, Siyuan hit them with three thousand iron cavalry and broke them, taking or killing on the order of twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，閻寶上言，定州節度使王處直為其子都幽於別室，都自稱留後。

translations.literal: On xinyou Yan Bao reported that Dingzhou commissioner Wang Chuzhi had been imprisoned by his son Du in a side room, and Du styled himself acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Yan Bao reported that Wang Chuzhi of Ding had been shut up by his son Du, who called himself acting commissioner.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：王處直叛附於契丹，其子都幽處直以來附。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》 says: Wang Chuzhi rebelled and went over to the Khitan; his son Du imprisoned Chuzhi and came over to submit.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Ouyang History》 says Chuzhi rebelled to the Khitan while Du locked up his father and submitted to Jin.)〉

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝至鎮州城下，張處瑾遣弟處琪、幕客齊儉等候帝乞降，言猶不遜，帝命囚之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, the Emperor reached below the walls of Zhen; Zhang Chujin sent his younger brother Chuqi and staff member Qi Jian to wait on the Emperor begging surrender, but their words were still insolent; the Emperor ordered them imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Cunxu camped under Zhen; Chujin sent his brother Chuqi and adviser Qi Jian to sue for terms with insolent speech, and he had them jailed.

sentences.zh: 時王師築土山以攻其壘，城中亦起土山以拒之，旬日之間，機巧百變。

translations.literal: The royal army then built earthen hills to assault their ramparts; inside the city they too raised hills to resist, and within ten days stratagems shifted a hundred ways.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raised siege mounds while the city countered with its own, and in ten days the engineers traded a hundred tricks.

sentences.zh: 張處瑾令韓正時以千騎夜突圍，將入定州與王處直議事，為我遊軍追擊，破之；

translations.literal: Zhang Chujin sent Han Zhengshi with a thousand horse to burst the encirclement by night, intending to reach Ding and consult with Wang Chuzhi; our roaming troops pursued and broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Chujin sent Han Zhengshi with a thousand horse to break out by night for Ding to see Chuzhi; Jin scouts ran them down;

sentences.zh: 餘眾保衡唐，賊將彭贇斬正時以降。

translations.literal: the remnant held Hengtang; the rebel officer Peng Zan beheaded Zhengshi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: the survivors held Hengtang until Peng Zan killed Zhengshi and came over.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛未，王鬱誘契丹安巴堅寇幽州，

translations.literal: Twelfth month, xinwei, Wang Yu induced the Khitan Anbajian to raid Youzhou,
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the twelfth month Wang Yu bribed the Khitan Anbajian to strike Youzhou,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》：王處直在定州，以鎮、定為唇齒，恐鎮亡而定孤，乃潛使人語其子王鬱，使賂契丹，令犯塞以救鎮州之圍。

translations.literal: (The 《Annals of the Khitan State》 says: Wang Chuzhi was at Dingzhou; because Zhen and Ding were lip and teeth, he feared that if Zhen fell Ding would stand alone; he secretly sent men to tell his son Wang Yu to bribe the Khitan to breach the frontier and relieve the siege of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Annals of the Khitan State》 says Chuzhi at Ding feared that with Zhen lost he would be isolated, and secretly told his son Yu to bribe the Khitan to raid the border and save Zhen.

sentences.zh: 王鬱說太祖曰：「鎮州美女如雲，金帛似山，天皇速往，則皆為己物也；

translations.literal: Wang Yu said to the Taizu emperor: "Zhenzhou has beauties like clouds and gold and silk like mountains; if the Heavenly Sovereign goes quickly, all will be his;
translations.idiomatic: Yu told the Khitan Taizu, "Zhen holds beauties like clouds and treasure like hills—march now and it is yours;

sentences.zh: 不然，則為晉王所有矣。

translations.literal: otherwise it will all belong to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: wait, and the Prince of Jin takes it."

sentences.zh: 」太祖以為然，率眾而南。）〉

translations.literal: " The Taizu thought it right and led his masses south.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed and marched south.)〉

sentences.zh: 遂引軍涿州，陷之。

translations.literal: He then led his army to Zhuozhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He drove on Zhuozhou and seized it.

sentences.zh: 又寇定州，王都遣使告急，帝自鎮州率五千騎赴之。

translations.literal: He also raided Dingzhou; Wang Du sent envoys reporting urgency, and the Emperor led five thousand horse from Zhen to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Ding as well; Du cried for help, and Cunxu rode from Zhen with five thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 天祐十九年春正月甲午，帝至新城，契丹前鋒三千騎至新樂。

translations.literal: Spring of Tianyou 19, first month, jiawu, the Emperor reached Xincheng; three thousand Khitan vanguard horse reached Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the first month of Tianyou 19 Cunxu reached Xincheng as three thousand Khitan van horse reached Xinle.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁將戴思遠乘虛以寇魏州，軍至魏店，李嗣源自領兵馳入魏州。

translations.literal: At that time Liang general Dai Siyuan seized the opening to raid Weizhou; his army reached Weidian; Li Siyuan himself led troops galloping into Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Dai Siyuan of Liang slipped in to raid Weizhou as far as Weidian; Li Siyuan raced into the city himself.

sentences.zh: 梁人知其有備，乃西渡洹水，陷成安而去。

translations.literal: The Liang men knew they were prepared and then crossed west over the Huan River, took Cheng'an, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Weizhou ready, Liang crossed the Huan west, sacked Cheng'an, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時契丹渡沙河，諸將相顧失色；

translations.literal: When the Khitan crossed the Sha River the generals looked at one another in dismay;
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan crossed the Sha the officers lost color;

sentences.zh: 又聞梁人內侵，鄴城危急，皆請旋師，唯帝謂不可，乃率親騎至新城。

translations.literal: hearing also that Liang had invaded within and Yecheng was critical, all begged to turn the army; only the Emperor said it could not be done, and he then led his personal horse to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: hearing Liang had struck within and Ye was in peril, all urged retreat—only Cunxu refused, and he led his personal horse to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 契丹萬餘騎，遽見帝軍，惶駭而退。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Khitan horse suddenly saw the Emperor's army and fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Khitan horse sighted Cunxu's line and bolted in panic.

sentences.zh: 帝分軍為二廣，追躡數十里，獲安巴堅之子。

translations.literal: The Emperor divided the army into two wings, pursued for several tens of li, and captured Anbajian's son.
translations.idiomatic: He split his force in two wings, chased tens of li, and took Anbajian's son.

sentences.zh: 時沙河冰薄，橋梁隘狹，敵爭踐而過，陷溺者甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time the Sha's ice was thin and the bridges narrow; the enemy scrambled across and many who trampled through fell in and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The Sha ice was thin and the bridges narrow; Khitan crowded the crossings and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 阿保機方在定州，聞前軍敗，退保望都。

translations.literal: Abaoji was then at Dingzhou; hearing the van had been beaten, he withdrew to hold Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji was at Ding; when he heard the van had lost, he fell back on Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 帝至定州，王都迎謁。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Dingzhou; Wang Du came out to welcome and pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu reached Ding and Du came out to greet him.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宿於開元寺。

translations.literal: That night he lodged at Kaiyuan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slept at Kaiyuan Temple.

sentences.zh: 翌日，引軍至望都，契丹逆戰。

translations.literal: Next day he led the army to Wangdu; the Khitan met them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he marched on Wangdu and the Khitan gave battle.

sentences.zh: 帝身先士伍，馳擊數四，敵退而結陣，帝之徒兵亦陣於水次。

translations.literal: The Emperor took the lead among the ranks, charged four or five times, the enemy withdrew and formed ranks, and the Emperor's foot soldiers also formed ranks at the water's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu led from the front, charged again and again until the Khitan drew up, and his foot formed line on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭躍馬奮擊，敵眾大潰，俘斬數千，追擊至易水，獲氈裘、毳幕、羊馬不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao leaped his horse and struck fiercely; the enemy masses broke in great rout; several thousand were captured or beheaded; pursuit reached the Yi River; felt coats, felt tents, sheep, and horses were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao spurred in and shattered them, taking thousands of heads to the Yi River and herds of sheep, horses, tents, and furs beyond count.

sentences.zh: 時歲且北至，大雪平地五尺，敵乏芻糧，人馬斃踣道路，累累不絕，帝乘勝追襲至幽州。

translations.literal: The year was nearing the winter solstice; heavy snow lay five chi deep on level ground; the enemy lacked fodder and grain; men and horses collapsed and fell along the road in unbroken lines; the Emperor pressed the pursuit in victory as far as Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With the solstice near, snow stood five feet deep on the plain; the Khitan ran out of fodder and horses and men dropped along the road; Cunxu chased in triumph to Youzhou.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》：晉王趨望都，為契丹所圍，力戰，出入數四，不解。

translations.literal: (The 《Records of the Khitan Kingdom》: The Prince of Jin hurried toward Wangdu and was surrounded by the Khitan; he fought fiercely, going in and out four times, but the siege was not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of the Khitan Kingdom》 says the Prince of Jin pressed on Wangdu, was ringed by the Khitan, and fought in and out four times without breaking free.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭引三百騎橫擊之，晉王始得出，因縱兵奮擊，太祖兵敗，遂北至易州。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao led three hundred horse in a flanking strike; only then did the Prince of Jin get out, and he then loosed his troops in a fierce attack; the Taizu's army was beaten and fled north as far as Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao charged in with three hundred horse and cut the Prince of Jin free; he then drove the attack home, routed the Liang Taizu's host, and chased them to Yi.

sentences.zh: 會大雪彌旬，平地數尺，人馬死者相屬，太祖乃歸。）〉

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell for more than ten days; on level ground it stood several feet; men and horses died in ranks along the road; the Taizu then returned.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell for ten days and piled several feet deep; men and horses died in heaps along the road, and the Taizu turned back.)〉

sentences.zh: 是月，梁將戴思遠寇德勝北城，築壘穿塹，地道雲梯，晝夜攻擊；

translations.literal: That month Liang general Dai Siyuan raided Desheng's north city, built stockades and dug trenches, used tunnels and scaling ladders, and attacked day and night;
translations.idiomatic: That month Dai Siyuan of Liang struck Desheng's north wall, threw up ramparts and trenches, tunneled and raised ladders, and assaulted without pause;

sentences.zh: 李存審極力拒守，城中危急。

translations.literal: Li Cunxu defended with all his strength; within the city the peril was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxu held with everything he had, and the city was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 帝自幽州聞之，倍道兼行以赴，梁人聞帝至，燒營而遁。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard from Youzhou he doubled his march to the rescue; hearing the Emperor had come, the Liang men burned their camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Word from Youzhou brought the Emperor at forced march; the Liang heard he was near, torched their camp, and ran.

sentences.zh: 三月丙午，王師敗於鎮州城下，閻寶退保趙州。

translations.literal: Third month, bingwu, the imperial army was defeated below Zhenzhou; Yan Bao withdrew to hold Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the third month the court army was beaten under Zhenzhou, and Yan Bao fell back to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 時鎮州累月受圍，城中艱食，王師築壘環之；

translations.literal: At that time Zhenzhou had been besieged for months; food in the city ran short; the imperial army built stockades ringing the walls;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou had been under siege for months with food running out; the court army had ringed it with camps;

sentences.zh: 又決滹沱水以絕城中出路。

translations.literal: and they also broke the Hutuo River to cut off the city's escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: and had broken the Hutuo to cut off every way out.

sentences.zh: 是日，城中軍出，攻其長圍，皆奮力死戰，王師不能拒，引師而退。

translations.literal: That day the garrison sallied and struck the long encirclement; all fought to the death; the imperial army could not hold them off, drew back, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That day the garrison burst out on the siege lines and fought to the death; the court army could not stand, broke, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 鎮人壞其營壘，取其芻糧者累日。

translations.literal: The men of Zhen tore down the camps and carried off fodder and grain for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen men wrecked the camps and hauled away fodder and grain for days.

sentences.zh: 帝聞失律，即以昭義節度使李嗣昭為北面招討使，進攻鎮州。

translations.literal: The Emperor, hearing of the setback, at once made Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao northern campaign commander and ordered him to press the attack on Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, the Emperor made Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi northern campaign commander and sent him back on Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，嗣昭為流矢所中，卒於師。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Sizhao was struck by a stray arrow and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Sizhao took a stray arrow and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 己卯，天平節度使閻寶卒。

translations.literal: On jimao Tianping military commissioner Yan Bao died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Yan Bao, commissioner of Tianping, died.

sentences.zh: 以振武節度使李存進為北面招討使。

translations.literal: Zhenwu military commissioner Li Cunjin was made northern campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunjin of Zhenwu was made northern campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 是月，大同軍節度使李存璋卒。

translations.literal: That month Datong military commissioner Li Cunzhang died.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Cunzhang of Datong died.

sentences.zh: 五月乙酉，李存進圍鎮州，營於東渡。

translations.literal: Fifth month, yiyou, Li Cunjin besieged Zhenzhou and encamped at Dongdu ford.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the fifth month Cunjin laid siege to Zhenzhou and camped at Dongdu crossing.

sentences.zh: 八月，梁將段凝陷衛州，刺史李存儒被擒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Liang general Duan Ning took Wei prefecture; prefect Li Cunru was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Duan Ning of Liang took Wei; Prefect Li Cunru was seized.

sentences.zh: 存儒，本俳優也，帝以其有膂力，故用為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: Cunru had originally been a performer; the Emperor used him for his strength and therefore made him Wei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Cunru had been a performer; the Emperor valued his brawn and made him prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 既而誅斂無度，人皆怨之，故為梁人所襲。

translations.literal: Afterward he levied without measure and all resented him, and so he was taken in a Liang raid.
translations.idiomatic: He then taxed without limit until the people hated him, and the Liang took him in a surprise strike.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙季良傳》：莊宗入鄴，時兵革屢興，屬邑租賦逋久。

translations.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Zhao Jiliang》: When Zhuangzong entered Ye, the army had risen again and again and the districts' rents and levies were long overdue.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Nine States Chronicle · Biography of Zhao Jiliang》 says when Zhuangzong entered Ye the armies had been in the field for years and district taxes were far in arrears.

sentences.zh: 一日，莊宗召季良切責之，季良對曰：「殿下何時平河南？

translations.literal: One day Zhuangzong summoned Jiliang and sharply reproved him; Jiliang replied: "When will Your Highness pacify the south of the River?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Zhuangzong called Jiliang in and rebuked him sharply. Jiliang said, "When will Your Highness finish the south of the River?"

sentences.zh: 」莊宗正色曰：「爾掌輿賦而稽緩，安問我勝負乎！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong said sternly: "You hold the transport levies yet delay—how dare you ask me about victory or defeat!"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong's face hardened: "You hold the grain rolls and drag your feet—who are you to ask me about the war?"

sentences.zh: 」季良曰：「殿下方謀攻守，復務急征，一旦眾心有變，恐河南非殿下所有。

translations.literal: " Jiliang said: "Your Highness is plotting attack and defense yet also presses for urgent collection; if the host's hearts shift in a day, I fear the south of the River will not be yours."
translations.idiomatic: " Jiliang said, "You are fighting for the south yet squeezing the districts—if the army turns in a day, the south of the River may not be yours."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗斂容前席曰：「微君之言，幾失吾大計！」）〉

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong composed his face and leaned forward on his mat: "But for your words I would nearly have lost my great plan!"）〉
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong softened and leaned forward: "Without your counsel I would have wrecked the whole plan!"）〉

sentences.zh: 梁將戴思遠又陷共城、新鄉等邑。

translations.literal: Liang general Dai Siyuan again took Gong city, Xinxiang, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan of Liang took Gong, Xinxiang, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 自是，澶淵之西，相州之南，皆為梁人所據。

translations.literal: From then on, west of Chanyuan and south of Xiangzhou, all fell to the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: From then on everything west of Chanyuan and south of Xiang was Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅朔，張處球悉城中兵奄至東垣渡，急攻我之壘門。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the new moon wuyin, Zhang Chuqiu led all the troops in the city in a sudden rush to the east wall ford and fiercely attacked our stockade gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin new moon of the ninth month Zhang Chuqiu hurled every man in the city on our camp gate at the east wall ford.

sentences.zh: 時騎軍已臨賊城，不覺其出，李存進惶駭，引十餘人鬥於橋上，賊退，我之騎軍前後夾擊之，賊眾大敗，步兵數千，殆無還者。

translations.literal: At that time the cavalry had already closed on the rebel city and did not notice them coming out; Li Cunjin in alarm led a little more than ten men to fight on the bridge; the rebels fell back; our cavalry before and behind pincered them; the rebel host was routed; several thousand foot soldiers scarcely one returned.
translations.idiomatic: Our horse were already at the walls and missed the sortie; Cunjin in alarm fought on the bridge with a dozen men; the rebels gave way; our cavalry struck from front and rear; thousands of foot were cut down and few came back.

sentences.zh: 是役也，李存進戰歿於師，以蕃漢馬步總管李存審為北面招討使，以攻鎮州。

translations.literal: In this battle Li Cunjin died fighting; Li Cunxu, overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot, was made northern campaign commander to attack Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjin fell in the fight; Li Cunxu, overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot, became northern campaign commander and pressed Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午夜，趙將李再豐之子衝投縋以接王師，諸軍登城，遲明畢入，鎮州平。

translations.literal: At midnight on bingwu the Zhao officer Li Zaifeng's son Chong let himself down by rope to meet the imperial army; the troops climbed the wall; by first light all were inside and Zhenzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on bingwu Li Zaifeng's son Chong slid down a rope to the court army; the troops scaled the wall, and by dawn Zhenzhou had fallen.

sentences.zh: 獲處球、處瑾、處琪並其母，及同惡高濛李翥、齊儉等，皆折足送行台，鎮人請醢而食之；

translations.literal: Chuqiu, Chujin, Chuqi, and their mother were taken, together with the ringleaders Gao Meng, Li Zhu, Qi Jian, and others; all had their feet broken and were sent to the field headquarters; the men of Zhen asked that they be minced and eaten;
translations.idiomatic: Chuqiu, Chujin, Chuqi, their mother, and ringleaders including Gao Meng, Li Zhu, and Qi Jian were seized, their feet broken, and sent to headquarters; the Zhen people begged to mince them for food;

sentences.zh: 發張文禮屍，磔於市。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli's corpse was dug up and dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli's corpse was dug up and torn apart in the market.

sentences.zh: 帝以符習為鎮州節度使，烏震為趙州刺史，趙仁貞為深州刺史，李再豐為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Fu Xi Zhenzhou military commissioner, Wu Zhen Zhao prefect, Zhao Renzhen Shen prefect, and Li Zaifeng Ji prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Fu Xi commissioner of Zhen, Wu Zhen prefect of Zhao, Zhao Renzhen prefect of Shen, and Li Zaifeng prefect of Ji.

sentences.zh: 鎮人請帝兼領本鎮，從之，乃以符習遙領天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: The men of Zhen asked the Emperor also to hold the circuit himself; he agreed, and Fu Xi was made Tianping military commissioner at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked the Emperor to hold the circuit himself; he agreed and kept Fu Xi as titular commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 十一月，河東監軍張承業卒。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Hedong army supervisor Zhang Chengye died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Chengye, Hedong army supervisor, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以魏州觀察判官張憲權知鎮州軍州事。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Weizhou observation judge Zhang Xian was made acting Zhenzhou military and civil commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhang Xian, Wei observation judge, was made acting commissioner of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 三月己卯，以橫海軍節度使、內外蕃漢馬步總管李存審為幽州節度使。

translations.literal: Third month, jimao, Bohai military commissioner and overall commander of inner and outer Tangut and Han horse and foot Li Cunxu was made Youzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the third month Li Cunxu of Bohai, overall commander of inner and outer Tangut and Han horse and foot, became commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 潞州留後李繼韜叛，送款於梁。

translations.literal: Luzhou acting prefect Li Jitao rebelled and sent allegiance to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jitao, acting prefect of Lu, rebelled and offered himself to Liang.

sentences.zh: 是月，築即位壇於魏州牙城之南。

translations.literal: That month an accession altar was built south of the Weizhou headquarters city.
translations.idiomatic: That month an accession altar was raised south of the Weizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己巳，帝升壇，祭告昊天上帝，遂即皇帝位，文武臣僚稱賀。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jisi, the Emperor ascended the altar, offered sacrifice and reported to August Heaven, then assumed the imperial throne; civil and military officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Emperor mounted the altar, sacrificed to Heaven, and took the throne; civil and military officials hailed him.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，禦應天門宣製：改天佑二十年為同光元年，大赦天下，自四月二十五日昧爽以前，除十惡五逆、放火行劫、持杖殺人、官典犯贓、屠牛鑄錢、合造毒藥外，罪無輕重，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: When the rites were done he went to the Yingtian Gate and proclaimed: Tianyou 20 was changed to Tongguang 1; a great amnesty was declared for all under Heaven; from before dawn on the twenty-fifth of the fourth month, except for the ten abominations, five capital crimes, arson, armed robbery, murder with a staff, official corruption, slaughtering cattle, coining money, and compounding poison, crimes great and small were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended he proclaimed at the Yingtian Gate that Tianyou 20 became Tongguang 1 and declared a great amnesty: before dawn on the twenty-fifth of the fourth month, save the ten abominations, five capital crimes, arson, robbery, murder with a weapon, official graft, cattle slaughter, coining, and poison-making, all crimes were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 應蕃漢馬步將校並賜功臣名號，超授檢校官，已高者與一子六品正員官，兵士並賜等第優給。

translations.literal: Tangut and Han horse and foot commanders were all granted meritorious titles, promoted to acting palace offices, those already high were given one son a sixth-rank regular post, and soldiers were all given graded bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut and Han commanders received merit titles and acting palace ranks; the highest won a son a sixth-rank post, and every soldier a graded bounty.

sentences.zh: 其戰歿功臣各加追贈，仍賜諡號。

translations.literal: Fallen meritorious officers each received posthumous promotion and were also granted posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Fallen officers were raised in rank posthumously and given posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 民年八十已上，與免一子役。

translations.literal: Commoners eighty years and above were granted exemption from one son's corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women eighty and older won exemption from one son's labor levy.

sentences.zh: 內外文武職官，並可直言極諫，無有隱諱。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials within and without might speak bluntly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Every civil and military officer, inside court and out, was invited to speak plainly without fear.

sentences.zh: 貢、選二司，宜令有司速商量施行。

translations.literal: The tribute and selection offices were ordered to have the responsible bureaus deliberate and put measures into effect at once.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute and selection offices were told to have the bureaus settle rules and act on them quickly.

sentences.zh: 雲、應、蔚、朔、易、定、幽、燕及山後八軍，秋夏稅率量與蠲減。

translations.literal: Yun, Ying, Wei, Shuo, Yi, Ding, You, Yan, and the eight armies behind the mountains had their summer and autumn tax rates measured and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Summer and autumn taxes were cut for Yun, Ying, Wei, Shuo, Yi, Ding, You, Yan, and the eight garrisons behind the mountains.

sentences.zh: 民有三世已上不分居者，與免雜徭。

translations.literal: Households of three generations or more not living apart were granted exemption from miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Families of three generations under one roof were freed from miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 諸道應有祥瑞，不用聞奏。

translations.literal: All circuits were told not to report auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits were told not to report lucky signs.

sentences.zh: 赦書有所未該，委所司條奏以聞雲。

translations.literal: What the amnesty did not cover was left to the offices to set out in memorial and report.
translations.idiomatic: Gaps in the amnesty were left to the offices to list and report up.

sentences.zh: 是歲，自正月不雨，人心憂恐，宣赦之日，澍雨溥降。

translations.literal: That year from the first month there had been no rain and hearts were fearful; on the day the amnesty was proclaimed timely rain fell in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had failed since the first month and people were afraid; the day the amnesty was read, soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 初，唐咸通中，金、水、土、火四星聚於畢、昴，太史奏：「畢、昴，趙、魏之分，其下將有王者。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Xiantong era of Tang, the metal, water, earth, and fire planets gathered in Bi and Mao; the court astronomer memorialized: "Bi and Mao are the allotment of Zhao and Wei; below them a king will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, in Tang's Xiantong era, metal, water, earth, and fire met in Bi and Mao; the astronomer reported, "Bi and Mao are Zhao and Wei's stars—a king will rise there."

sentences.zh: 」懿宗乃詔令鎮州王景崇被袞冕攝朝三日，遣臣下備儀注、軍府稱臣以厭之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yizong then ordered Wang Jingchong of Zhenzhou to wear imperial robes and regalia and hold court for three days as regent, and sent his ministers with full ritual and the military government to submit as subjects to avert the omen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yizong made Wang Jingchong of Zhen wear imperial robes for three days, sent ministers with full rites, and had the army submit as subjects to ward off the sign.

sentences.zh: 其後四十九年，帝破梁軍於柏鄉，平定趙、魏，至是即位於鄴宮。

translations.literal: Forty-nine years later the Emperor broke the Liang army at Baixiang, pacified Zhao and Wei, and now took the throne at the Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-nine years later the Emperor routed Liang at Baixiang, pacified Zhao and Wei, and now enthroned himself at Ye.

sentences.zh: 是月，以行台左丞相豆盧革為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、太清宮使；

translations.literal: That month left chief minister of the field headquarters Dou Lu Ge was made vice director of the Secretariat, joint director of the Chancellery, and commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace;
translations.idiomatic: That month Dou Lu Ge, left chief of the field headquarters, became vice director of the Secretariat, joint chancellor, and commissioner of the Grand Pure Palace;

sentences.zh: 以行台右丞相盧澄為中書侍郎平章事、監修國史；

translations.literal: right chief minister Lu Cheng was made vice director of the Secretariat with chancellor rank and commissioner for compiling the national history;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng, right chief, became vice director of the Secretariat with chancellor rank and commissioner for the national history;

sentences.zh: 以前定州掌書記李德休為御史中丞；

translations.literal: former Dingzhou secretarial aide Li Detiu was made censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: former Ding secretarial aide Li Detiu became censor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 以河東節度判官盧質為兵部尚書，充翰林學士承旨；

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner judge Lu Zhi was made minister of war and chief Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong judge Lu Zhi became minister of war and chief Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以河東掌書記馮道為戶部侍郎，充翰林學士；

translations.literal: Hedong secretarial aide Feng Dao was made vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong secretary Feng Dao became vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以魏博、鎮冀觀察判官張憲為工部侍郎，充租庸使；

translations.literal: Wei-Bo and Zhen-Ji observation judge Zhang Xian was made vice minister of works and grain transport commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Bo and Zhen-Ji judge Zhang Xian became vice minister of works and grain transport commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以中門使郭崇韜、昭義監軍使張居翰並為樞密使；

translations.literal: inner gate commissioner Guo Chongtao and Zhaoyi army supervisor Zhang Juhun were both made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: inner gate commissioner Guo Chongtao and Zhaoyi army supervisor Zhang Juhun both became commissioners of military affairs;

sentences.zh: 以權知幽州軍府事李紹宏為宣徽使；

translations.literal: acting Youzhou military commissioner Li Shaohong was made palace commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: acting Youzhou commissioner Li Shaohong became palace commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以魏博節度判官王正言為禮部尚書，行興唐尹；

translations.literal: Wei-Bo military commissioner judge Wang Zhengyan was made minister of rites and acting Xingxing prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Wei-Bo judge Wang Zhengyan became minister of rites and acting Xingxing prefect;

sentences.zh: 以河東軍城都虞候孟知祥為太原尹，充西京副留守；

translations.literal: Hedong capital garrison commandant Meng Zhixiang was made Taiyuan prefect and deputy western capital defender;
translations.idiomatic: Hedong garrison commandant Meng Zhixiang became Taiyuan prefect and deputy western capital defender;

sentences.zh: 以澤潞節度判官任圓為工部尚書兼真定尹，充北京副留守。

translations.literal: Zelu military commissioner judge Ren Yuan was made minister of works and acting Zhending prefect, deputy northern capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: Zelu judge Ren Yuan became minister of works, acting Zhending prefect, and deputy northern capital defender.

sentences.zh: 詔升魏州為東京興唐府，改元城縣為興唐縣，貴鄉縣為廣晉縣，以太原為西京，以鎮州為北都。

translations.literal: An edict raised Weizhou to the eastern capital Xingxing prefecture, changed Yuancheng county to Xingxing county and Guixiang county to Guangjin county, made Taiyuan the western capital, and made Zhenzhou the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Weizhou the eastern capital Xingxing, renamed Yuancheng to Xingxing and Guixiang to Guangjin, set Taiyuan as western capital and Zhenzhou as northern capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，所管節度一十三，州五十。

translations.literal: At that time there were thirteen military circuits and fifty prefectures under rule.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then held thirteen circuits and fifty prefectures.

sentences.zh: 閏月丁丑，以李嗣源為檢校侍中，依前橫海軍節度使、內外蕃漢副總管；

translations.literal: Intercalary month, dingchou, Li Siyuan was made acting palace attendant and continued as Bohai military commissioner and inner and outer Tangut and Han deputy overall commander;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the intercalary month Li Siyuan became acting palace attendant, remaining Bohai commissioner and inner and outer Tangut and Han deputy overall commander;

sentences.zh: 以幽州節度使李存審為檢校太師、兼中書令，依前蕃漢馬步總管；

translations.literal: Youzhou military commissioner Li Cunxu was made acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, continuing as overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxu of Youzhou became acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, still overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;

sentences.zh: 以河東節度使朱友謙為檢校太師、兼尚書令。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Zhu Youqian was made acting grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian of Hedong became acting grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安國軍節度使符習加同平章事，定州節度使王都加檢校侍中。

translations.literal: Anguo military commissioner Fu Xi was given joint chancellor rank, and Dingzhou military commissioner Wang Du was made acting palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi of Anguo received joint chancellor rank; Wang Du of Ding became acting palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 是月，追尊曾祖蔚州太保為昭烈皇帝，廟號懿祖；

translations.literal: That month the great-great-grandfather, Grand Protector of Weizhou, was posthumously honored as Illustrious Liege Emperor, temple name Yizu;
translations.idiomatic: That month the great-great-grandfather, grand protector of Wei, was raised as Illustrious Liege Emperor, temple name Yizu;

sentences.zh: 夫人崔氏曰昭列皇后。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was titled Illustrious Array Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was named Illustrious Array Empress.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇祖代州太保為文景皇帝，廟號獻祖；

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather, Grand Protector of Daizhou, was posthumously honored as Cultured Splendor Emperor, temple name Xianzu;
translations.idiomatic: The grandfather, grand protector of Dai, was raised as Cultured Splendor Emperor, temple name Xianzu;

sentences.zh: 夫人秦氏曰文景皇后。

translations.literal: Lady Qin was titled Cultured Splendor Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qin was named Cultured Splendor Empress.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇考河東節度使、太師、中書令、晉王為武皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: The imperial father, Hedong military commissioner, grand preceptor, director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Jin, was posthumously honored as Martial Emperor, temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The father, Hedong commissioner, grand preceptor, chancellor, and Prince of Jin, was raised as Martial Emperor, temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 詔於晉陽立宗廟，以高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文皇帝、懿宗昭聖皇帝、昭宗聖穆皇帝及懿祖以下為七廟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered an ancestral temple raised at Jinyang with the shrines of High Ancestor Shenyao, Taizong the Cultured, Yizong the Illustrious Sage, and Zhaozong the Sagely Mournful, together with Yizu and below, making seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: An edict built a temple at Jinyang with Shenyao, Taizong, Yizong, Zhaozong, and the new ancestors from Yizu down—seven halls in all.

sentences.zh: 甲午，契丹寇幽州，至易、定而還。

translations.literal: On jiawu the Khitan raided Youzhou and reached Yi and Ding before turning back.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Khitan struck Youzhou, reached Yi and Ding, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時有自鄆來者，言節度使戴思遠領兵在河上，州城無守兵，可襲而取之。

translations.literal: At that time someone from Yan reported that military commissioner Dai Siyuan was on the river with his troops and the prefectural city had no garrison— it could be taken in a surprise stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Word came from Yan that Dai Siyuan was on the river with his army and Yan city lay undefended—a sudden strike could take it.

sentences.zh: 帝召李嗣源謀曰：「昭義阻命，梁將董璋攻迫澤州，梁志在澤、潞，不慮別有事生，汶陽無備，不可失也。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Li Siyuan to plan and said: "Zhaoyi defies orders; Liang general Dong Zhang presses Ze prefecture; the Liang aim is Ze and Lu and they do not expect another move—Wenyang is unguarded and must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called Li Siyuan and said, "Zhaoyi is in revolt and Dong Zhang of Liang is hammering Ze; they have eyes only for Ze and Lu and will not look for trouble elsewhere—Wenyang is open and we must not miss it."

sentences.zh: 」嗣源以為然。

translations.literal: " Siyuan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Siyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，命嗣源率步騎五千，箝枚自河趨鄆。

translations.literal: On renyin he ordered Siyuan to lead five thousand foot and horse, branches in their mouths, and hurry along the river toward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he sent Siyuan with five thousand foot and horse, branches in their mouths, racing along the river on Yan.

sentences.zh: 是夜陰雨，我師至城下，鄆人不覺，遂乘城而入，鄆州平。

translations.literal: That night rain fell in the dark; our army reached below the wall and the men of Yan did not notice; they climbed the wall and entered, and Yan prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell that night; the army came under the walls unseen, scaled them, and Yan fell before dawn.

sentences.zh: 製以李嗣源為天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: By proclamation Li Siyuan was made Tianping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A proclamation made Li Siyuan commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 梁主聞鄆州陷，大恐，乃遣王彥章代戴思遠總兵以來拒。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler, hearing Yan had fallen, was greatly afraid and sent Wang Yanzhang to replace Dai Siyuan as overall commander and come to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler, hearing Yan was lost, panicked and sent Wang Yanzhang to replace Dai Siyuan and block the advance.

sentences.zh: 時朱守殷守德勝南城，帝懼彥章奔衝，遂幸澶州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Shouyin held Desheng's south city; the Emperor feared Yanzhang would strike in a rush and therefore went in person to Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin held Desheng's south wall; fearing Yanzhang would burst through, the Emperor went to Chanyuan himself.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉，彥章夜率舟師自楊村浮河而下，斷德勝之浮橋，攻南城，陷之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, xinyou, Yanzhang by night led boat troops down from Yangcun on the floating river, cut Desheng's pontoon bridge, attacked the south city, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the fifth month Yanzhang led boats by night from Yangcun down the river, severed Desheng's pontoon, stormed the south city, and took it.

sentences.zh: 帝令中書焦彥賓馳至楊劉，固守其城；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Secretariat director Jiao Yanbin to gallop to Yangliu and hold the city fast;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent chancellor Jiao Yanbin at full gallop to hold Yangliu;

sentences.zh: 令朱守殷撤德勝北城屋木攻具，浮河而下，以助楊劉。

translations.literal: he ordered Zhu Shouyin to strip Desheng's north city of house timbers and siege gear and float them downriver to aid Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Zhu Shouyin to strip Desheng's north wall of timber and engines and float them down to Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 是時，德勝軍食芻茭薪炭數十萬計，至是令人輦負入澶州，事既倉卒，耗失殆半。

translations.literal: At that time Desheng's army stores held fodder, reeds, and charcoal in the hundreds of thousands; now men were made to carry them on their backs into Chanyuan; the work was rushed and nearly half was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng then held fodder, reeds, and charcoal by the hundred thousand loads; men were rushed to haul it to Chanyuan and nearly half was lost in the scramble.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷以所毀屋木編筏，置步軍於其上。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin lashed the wrecked house timbers into rafts and set foot soldiers on them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin bound the wrecked timbers into rafts and put foot soldiers aboard.

sentences.zh: 王彥章以舟師沿流而下，各行一岸，每遇轉灘水彙，即中流交鬥，流矢雨集，或全舟覆沒，一彼一此，終日百戰，比及楊劉，殆亡其半。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang's boat troops drifted down with the current, each side of the river one file; whenever they met a bend where the water piled up they fought in midstream; arrows fell like rain; sometimes whole boats were sunk; first one side then the other battled all day; by the time they reached Yangliu nearly half were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang's boats drifted down, one line on each bank; at every bend they fought in midstream under a rain of arrows, boats sinking whole; the duel lasted all day, and by Yangliu nearly half were gone.

sentences.zh: 己巳，王彥章、段凝率大軍攻楊劉南城，焦彥賓與守城將李周極力固守。

translations.literal: On jisi Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning led a great army to attack Yangliu's south city; Jiao Yanbin and the defending general Li Zhou defended with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Yanzhang and Duan Ning stormed Yangliu's south wall; Jiao Yanbin and Li Zhou held with everything they had.

sentences.zh: 梁軍晝夜攻擊，百道齊進，竟不能下，遂結營於楊劉之南，東西延袤十數柵。

translations.literal: The Liang army attacked day and night, a hundred paths at once, yet could not take it; they then pitched camp south of Yangliu, east and west stretching more than ten stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Liang assaulted day and night along a hundred lines and still could not enter; they camped south of Yangliu in a line of more than ten stockades.

sentences.zh: 六月己亥，帝親禦軍至楊劉，登城望見梁軍，重壕復壘，以絕其路，帝乃選勇士持短兵出戰。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jihai, the Emperor personally led the army to Yangliu, climbed the wall, and saw the Liang host with deep trenches and double ramparts cutting off the roads; he then chose brave men with short weapons to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the sixth month the Emperor came to Yangliu in person, mounted the wall, saw Liang trenches and double ramparts choking every road, and sent picked men with short weapons to sally.

sentences.zh: 梁軍於城門外，連延屈曲，穿掘小壕，伏甲士於中，候帝軍至，則弓弩齊發，師人多傷矢，不得進。

translations.literal: Outside the city gate the Liang army wound in curves, dug small trenches, and hid armored men within; when the imperial army came bows and crossbows fired together; many in the host were wounded by arrows and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate Liang had dug zigzag trenches and hidden armored men; when the court army came crossbows volleyed together, many fell, and the line could not move.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，問計於郭崇韜；

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled and asked Guo Chongtao for a plan;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was vexed and asked Guo Chongtao for counsel;

sentences.zh: 崇韜請於下流據河築壘，以救鄆州。

translations.literal: Chongtao asked to build stockades downriver on the river to relieve Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao urged stockades downriver on the Yellow River to save Yan.

sentences.zh: 又請帝日令勇士挑戰，旬日之內，寇若不至，營壘必成。

translations.literal: He also asked the Emperor to have brave men challenge daily; within ten days, if the enemy did not come, the fortified camp would surely be completed.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the Emperor to send champions out to fight every day; if the enemy stayed away ten days, the fort would stand.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，即令崇韜與毛璋率數千人中夜往博州濟河東，晝夜督役，居六日，營壘將成。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, at once ordered Chongtao and Mao Zhang to lead several thousand men at midnight from Bozhou to cross east of the river, supervising labor day and night; in six days the camp was nearly finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and sent Chongtao and Mao Zhang with several thousand men at midnight from Bozhou across the river to the east bank, pressing the work night and day; in six days the works were nearly done.

sentences.zh: 戊子，梁將王彥章、杜晏球領徒數萬，晨壓帝之新壘。

translations.literal: Day wuzi, Liang generals Wang Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu led tens of thousands and at dawn pressed the Emperor's new fort.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Wang Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu of Liang brought tens of thousands and at dawn drove on the Emperor's new camp.

sentences.zh: 時板築雖畢，牆仞低庳，戰具未備，沙城散惡，王彥章列騎環城，虐用其人，使步軍堙壕登堞。

translations.literal: At that time although rammed-earth work was finished, the wall height was low and cramped, war gear was not ready, and the sand ramparts were loose and poor; Wang Yanzhang arrayed cavalry around the city, cruelly used the people, and had foot soldiers fill the moat and climb the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: The tamped earth was up but the walls were low and weak, weapons were not ready, and the sandworks were rotten; Yanzhang ringed the place with horse, drove the people cruelly to fill the ditch and scale the wall.

sentences.zh: 又於上流下巨艦十餘艘，扼斷濟路。

translations.literal: He also placed more than ten great ships upstream to choke off the crossing route.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream he posted more than ten great ships to block the crossing.

sentences.zh: 自旦至午，攻擊百端，城中危急。

translations.literal: From dawn to noon attacks came from every side; inside the city the peril was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: From morning to noon they struck from every quarter and the city was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 帝自楊劉引軍陣於西岸，城中望之，大呼，帝艤舟將渡，梁軍遂解圍，退保鄒家口。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the army from Yangliu and formed battle lines on the west bank; those in the city saw them and shouted loudly; the Emperor moored boats to cross, and the Liang army then lifted the siege and withdrew to hold Zoujiakou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marched from Yangliu and drew up on the west bank; the garrison saw him and cheered; he made to cross by boat and the Liang broke off and fell back on Zoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁未，帝御軍沿河而南，梁軍棄鄒家口夜遁，委棄鍋甲芻糧千計。

translations.literal: Seventh month of autumn, day dingwei, the Emperor led the army south along the river; the Liang army abandoned Zoujiakou and fled by night, casting away cauldrons, armor, hay, and grain by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the seventh month he led the host south along the river; the Liang quit Zoujiakou by night and left thousands of pots, armor, fodder, and grain behind.

sentences.zh: 戊午，遣騎將李紹貽直抵梁軍壘，梁益恐。

translations.literal: Day wuwu, he sent cavalry commander Li Shaoyi straight to the Liang camp; the Liang grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he sent the horse commander Li Shaoyi straight to the Liang lines and their fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 又聞李嗣源自鄆州引大軍將至，己未夜，梁軍拔營而遁，復保於楊村。

translations.literal: They also heard Li Siyuan was leading a great army from Yanzhou and would soon arrive; on the night of jiwei the Liang army pulled camp and fled, again holding Yangcun.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Li Siyuan was marching a great host from Yanzhou; that jiwei night the Liang struck camp and fled back to Yangcun.

sentences.zh: 帝軍屯於德勝。

translations.literal: The Emperor's army encamped at Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's host halted at Desheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝幸楊劉城，巡視梁軍故壘。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, the Emperor visited Yangliu city and inspected the Liang army's former camps.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he went to Yangliu and walked the old Liang encampments.

sentences.zh: 八月壬申朔，帝遣李紹斌以甲士五千援澤州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, first day of the month renshen, the Emperor sent Li Shaobin with five thousand armored soldiers to relieve Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon in the eighth month he sent Li Shaobin with five thousand armored men to relieve Ze.

sentences.zh: 初，李繼韜之叛也，潞之舊將裴約以兵戍澤州，不徇韜之逆。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Jitao rebelled, the former Lu commander Pei Yue held Ze with troops and would not follow Jitao's treason.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jitao had rebelled, the old Lu officer Pei Yue garrisoned Ze and refused to join him.

sentences.zh: 既而梁遣董璋率眾攻其城，約拒守久之，告急於帝，故遣紹斌救之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Liang sent Dong Zhang with a host to attack the city; Yue held out a long time and begged the Emperor for aid, and so Shaobin was sent to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang then sent Dong Zhang against the city; Yue held long and cried to the Emperor for help, and Shaobin was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 未至而城已陷，裴約被害，帝聞之，嗟痛不已。

translations.literal: Before he arrived the city had already fallen and Pei Yue was killed; hearing it, the Emperor sighed in grief without end.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin had not yet arrived when the city fell and Yue was slain; the Emperor grieved without cease.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝自楊劉歸鄴。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu, the Emperor returned from Yangliu to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he went from Yangliu back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 梁以段凝代王彥章為帥。

translations.literal: The Liang made Duan Ning replace Wang Yanzhang as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang replaced Wang Yanzhang with Duan Ning as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 戊子，凝帥眾五萬結營於王村，自高陵渡河。

translations.literal: Day wuzi, Ning led fifty thousand men and encamped at Wang Village, crossing the river from Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Ning brought fifty thousand men to camp at Wang Village and crossed from Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 帝軍遇之，生擒梁前鋒軍士二百人，戮於都市。

translations.literal: The Emperor's army met them, captured alive two hundred Liang vanguard soldiers, and executed them in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin host met them, took two hundred Liang vanguard alive, and put them to death in the market.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝御軍至朝城。

translations.literal: Day gengyin, the Emperor led the army to Chaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he led the army to Chaocheng.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，梁左右先鋒指揮使康延孝領百騎來奔，帝虛懷引見，賜禦衣玉帶，屏人問之。

translations.literal: Day wuxu, Liang Left and Right Vanguard Commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect; the Emperor received him with open courtesy, granted imperial robe and jade belt, and dismissed attendants to question him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Kang Yanxiao, Liang commander of the Left and Right Vanguard, came over with a hundred riders; the Emperor welcomed him generously, gave him court robe and jade belt, and questioned him in private.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣竊觀汴人兵眾不少，論其君臣將校，則終見敗亡。

translations.literal: He replied: "I have privately observed that the men of Bian are not few in number, but considering their ruler, ministers, and officers, they will in the end be defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I have watched the Bian host: their numbers are great, but their ruler, ministers, and commanders are already doomed.

sentences.zh: 趙岩、趙鵠、張漢傑居中專政，締結宮掖，賄賂公行。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan, Zhao He, and Zhang Hanjie hold central power, tie themselves to the inner palace, and bribery runs openly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan, Zhao He, and Zhang Hanjie rule from the center, court the palace women, and buy every office.

sentences.zh: 段凝素無武略，一朝便見大用；

translations.literal: Duan Ning by nature has no martial art, yet overnight he was given great employment;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning has no military talent, yet overnight he commands all;

sentences.zh: 霍彥威、王彥章皆宿將有名，翻出其下。

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei and Wang Yanzhang are both veteran generals of renown, yet they are placed beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei and Wang Yanzhang are famous old commanders, yet they rank below him.

sentences.zh: 自彥章獲德勝南城，梁主亦稍獎使。

translations.literal: Since Yanzhang took Desheng's south city, the Liang ruler also slightly rewarded and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhang took Desheng's south city the Liang ruler gave him some favor again.

sentences.zh: 彥章立性剛暴，不耐淩製，梁主每一發軍，即令近臣監護，進止可否，悉取監軍處分，彥章悒悒，形於顏色。

translations.literal: Yanzhang's nature is fierce and brutal and he cannot bear control; each time the Liang ruler sent out the army he had close attendants supervise; whether to advance or halt was entirely decided by the supervisors—Yanzhang was depressed and it showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang is harsh and proud and hates oversight; every campaign the Liang ruler set eunuchs over him who ordered every move—Yanzhang brooded and his face showed it.

sentences.zh: 自河津失利，段凝、彥章又獻謀，欲數道舉軍，合董璋以陝虢、澤潞之眾，趨石會關以寇太原。

translations.literal: Since the defeat at the river crossing, Duan Ning and Yanzhang again offered a plan to raise armies on several routes: join Dong Zhang with the forces of Shaanxi-Guo and Ze-Lu and strike toward Shihui Pass to invade Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After the river defeat Ning and Yanzhang proposed a multi-pronged advance: Dong Zhang with Shaanxi-Guo and Ze-Lu would march on Shihui Pass against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 霍彥威統關西、汝、洛之眾自相衛以寇鎮定，段凝、杜晏球領大軍以當陛下，令王彥章、張漢傑統禁軍以攻鄆州，決取十月內大舉。

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei would command the Guanxi, Ru, and Luo troops from Xiangwei to raid Zhen and Ding; Duan Ning and Du Yanqiu would lead the main host against Your Majesty; Wang Yanzhang and Zhang Hanjie would command the forbidden army to attack Yanzhou—a great campaign was fixed for within the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei would take Guanxi, Ru, and Luo from Xiangwei against Zhen and Ding; Ning and Du Yanqiu would face Your Majesty; Yanzhang and Zhang Hanjie would lead the palace guard on Yanzhou—the grand stroke was set for before the tenth month ended.

sentences.zh: 又自滑州南決破河堤，使水東注曹、濮之間，至於汶陽，彌漫不絕，以陷北軍。

translations.literal: They would also breach the river dyke south of Huazhou so the water ran east between Cao and Pu as far as Wenyang, spreading without end to trap the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: They would break the dyke south of Huazhou and flood Cao and Pu to Wenyang without end to drown the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 臣在軍側聞此議。

translations.literal: I heard this plan at the army's side.
translations.idiomatic: I heard this plan in their camp.

sentences.zh: 臣惟汴人兵力，聚則不少，分則無餘。

translations.literal: I consider the strength of Bian: gathered together they are not few, but divided they have nothing left.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's strength gathered looks large, but split up it is nothing.

sentences.zh: 陛下但待分兵，領鐵騎五千，自鄆州兼程直抵於汴，不旬日，天下事定矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only wait until they divide their forces, then lead five thousand iron cavalry from Yanzhou by forced march straight to Bian; within ten days the empire will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they divide, then take five thousand iron horse from Yanzhou by forced march straight to Bian—in ten days the realm is yours.

sentences.zh: 」帝懌然壯之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased and heartened by it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and took heart.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅朔，帝在朝城，凝兵至臨河南，與帝之騎軍接戰。

translations.literal: Ninth month, first day renyin, the Emperor was at Chaocheng; Ning's army reached south of Linhe and clashed with the Emperor's cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin new moon in the ninth month he was at Chaocheng when Ning's troops came south of Linhe and fought his horse.

sentences.zh: 是時澤潞叛，衛州、黎陽為梁人所據，州以西、相以南，寇鈔日至，編戶流亡，計其軍賦，不支半年。

translations.literal: At that time Ze and Lu had rebelled; Weizhou and Liyang were held by the Liang; west of the prefecture and south of Xiang, enemy raids came daily and registered households fled; reckoned, military revenue would not last half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Lu were in revolt, Weizhou and Liyang were Liang, and west of Zhou and south of Xiang raiders came daily while taxpayers fled—supplies would not last six months.

sentences.zh: 又王鬱、盧文進召契丹南侵瀛、涿。

translations.literal: Also Wang Yu and Lu Wenjin summoned the Khitan south to raid Ying and Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu and Lu Wenjin also called the Khitan south against Ying and Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 及聞梁人將圖大舉，帝深憂之，召將吏謀其大計，或曰：「自我得汶陽以來，須大將固守，城門之外，元是賊疆，細而料之，得不如失。

translations.literal: When he heard the Liang were planning a great campaign the Emperor was deeply worried and summoned officers to debate the grand plan; some said: "Since we took Wenyang we have needed great generals to hold fast; beyond the gates was always enemy country—carefully weighed, the gain does not equal the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the Liang grand design he was deeply troubled and called his commanders; one said, "Since Wenyang fell we have had to post great generals to hold ground that was always enemy land—we have gained less than we hold.

sentences.zh: 今若馳檄告諭梁人，卻衛州、黎陽以易鄆州，指河為界，約且休兵。

translations.literal: Now if we dispatch a proclamation to tell the Liang, return Weizhou and Liyang in exchange for Yanzhou, take the river as border, and agree to a truce for the moment—
translations.idiomatic: Send a proclamation offering Weizhou and Liyang for Yanzhou, the river as border, and a truce for now—

sentences.zh: 我國力稍集，則議改圖。

translations.literal: when our state's strength is somewhat gathered, then we may reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: when our strength recovers we can plan again."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「嘻，行此謀則無葬地矣！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Alas! Carry out this plan and I shall have no place to be buried!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Foolishness! Do that and I shall have no grave!"

sentences.zh: 」時郭崇韜勸帝親禦六軍，直趨汴州，半月之間，天下可定。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao urged the Emperor to personally lead the six armies straight to Bianzhou; within half a month the empire could be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao then urged him to lead the six armies himself straight on Bian—in half a month the realm would be his.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「正合朕意。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That exactly fits my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is exactly my mind.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫得則為王，失則為寇，予行計決矣！

translations.literal: A great man who wins becomes king; who loses becomes a bandit—my plan is decided!"
translations.idiomatic: Win and be king, lose and be an outlaw—I have made up my mind!"

sentences.zh: 」又問司天監，對曰：「今歲時不利，深入必無成功。

translations.literal: He also asked the Director of Astronomy, who replied: "This year's season is unlucky; a deep advance will surely not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Director of Astronomy, who said, "The stars this year forbid it; a deep advance cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 」帝弗聽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，梁將王彥章率眾至汶河，李嗣源遣騎軍偵視，至遞公鎮，梁軍來挑戰，嗣源以精騎擊而敗之，生擒梁將任釗、田章等三百人，俘斬二百級，彥章引眾保於中都。

translations.literal: Day wuchen, Liang general Wang Yanzhang led his host to the Wen River; Li Siyuan sent cavalry to reconnoiter; at Digong post the Liang came out to challenge; Siyuan struck with elite cavalry and defeated them, capturing alive Liang generals Ren Zhao, Tian Zhang, and three hundred others, taking two hundred heads in battle; Yanzhang led his masses to hold Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Yanzhang of Liang reached the Wen; Li Siyuan sent scouts to Digong post; the Liang offered battle and Siyuan routed them with picked horse, taking Ren Zhao, Tian Zhang, and three hundred others alive and two hundred heads; Yanzhang fell back on Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 嗣源飛驛告捷，帝置酒大悅，曰：「是當決行渡河之策。

translations.literal: Siyuan sent a fast courier with the victory report; the Emperor set out wine and was greatly pleased, saying: "This is the time to decide on the plan to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan sent word by urgent post; the Emperor feasted in joy and said, "Now we must decide to cross the river."

sentences.zh: 」己巳，下令軍中將士家屬並令歸鄴。

translations.literal: Day jisi, he ordered that the families of officers and soldiers in the army all return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he ordered every soldier's family sent back to Ye.
